request.prompt: Which humanoid robots can be purchased in North America?

result.text:
Commercial and research-grade humanoid robots available for purchase, lease, or direct order in North America span several tiers—ranging from entry-level developer models to enterprise-scale industrial platforms.

1. Developer & Research Humanoids

Unitree G1

Type: Bipedal humanoid / developer platform
Approx. Price: From $13,500 USD (base model) or higher for EDU/Pro variants ($50,000–$64,000 via specialty distributors)
Where to get it: Orderable directly through the Unitree Official Store or specialized robotics vendors.

Unitree H1 / H2 Series

Type: Full-size bipedal humanoids
Approx. Price: $29,900 – $90,000+ USD (depending on the generation and EDU add-ons)
Where to get it: Available via Unitree Official Store or global industrial robotics brokers.

EngineAI T800 Pro

Type: Bipedal general-purpose humanoid
Approx. Price: $63,000 USD
Where to get it: Offered through North American commercial robotics distributors like Robots International.

2. Industrial & Commercial Deployment Humanoids

Agility Robotics Digit

Type: Bipedal logistics and warehouse humanoid
Approx. Price: $200,000 USD (direct purchase + deployment/software fees) or $8,500/month via a Robot-as-a-Service (RaaS) lease model.
Where to get it: Enterprise allocation and pilot-to-fleet leasing via Agility Robotics.

UBTECH Walker S2 / Cruzr Series

Type: Industrial/service humanoid
Approx. Price: $15,999 – $149,995 USD depending on service vs. industrial specs.
Where to get it: Available through select commercial automation suppliers.

3. Pilot Programs & Pre-Orders (Not Yet Off-the-Shelf)

Apptronik Apollo: Available strictly via enterprise pilot scoping (estimated deployment valuation up to $50,000).

Figure AI (Figure 01 / 02): Deployed through targeted commercial pilot partnerships (e.g., manufacturing and automotive testbeds) rather than public retail.

Tesla Optimus: Announced for future consumer/commercial tiers, with projected mass-market availability still pending further scale-up.

Are you looking for a robot for academic research/programming, a commercial/warehouse use case, or just exploring what's out there? I can dive deeper into specs, lead times, or software SDKs for any of these models.
